headline: The investigation indicates associations between specific sensors and failing runs, with modest predictive evidence from the model. Findings suggest that certain sensors may reflect underlying issues in the production process.

key_findings.text: 81 runs were flagged as anomalous, with a flag rate of 8.6% for failing runs compared to 4.9% for passing runs, resulting in a lift of 1.758.
Failing runs had an average of 14.058 sensors out of control limits, while passing runs had 12.202 sensors out of limits.
The sensor f_059 showed significant discrepancies, being out of limits in 25.0% of failing runs versus 9.9% of passing runs.

hypotheses.title: The sensor f_059 is associated with failing runs.
hypotheses.evidence: f_059 shows a significant difference in out-of-limit rates (25.0% for failing vs 9.9% for passing runs) with a q-value of 2.5e-08.
hypotheses.verify: Review equipment logs and maintenance records to correlate f_059 readings with failure events.

hypotheses.title: The sensor f_103 is associated with failing runs.
hypotheses.evidence: f_103 has a median of -0.0102 for passing runs compared to -0.0082 for failing runs, with a q-value of 2.1e-06.
hypotheses.verify: Conduct controlled experiments to isolate the effects of f_103 on production outcomes.

hypotheses.title: The sensor f_247 is associated with failing runs.
hypotheses.evidence: f_247 has a median of 0.0421 for failing runs compared to 0.0262 for passing runs, with a q-value of 0.00013.
hypotheses.verify: Analyze historical performance data of f_247 to assess its reliability and drift over time.

hypotheses.title: The average number of sensors out of control limits is associated with failing runs.
hypotheses.evidence: Failing runs had an average of 14.058 sensors out of limits compared to 12.202 for passing runs.
hypotheses.verify: Investigate flagged anomalous runs for common patterns or conditions leading to failures.
